subject.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode — the roadmap

question: Should OpenClaw accept Codex-style structured questions, plan mode, and goal-mode continuation as core runtime features now, and should the paired implementation land as one broad branch or be split into staged PRs?
rationale: The requested work changes core runtime behavior, gateway protocol/API surfaces, UI/channel delivery, and unattended goal semantics, so automation cannot decide the release shape or whether these primitives belong in core without maintainer intent.

options.title: Stage the rollout
options.body: Keep this hub open and require focused question, plan, and goal PRs or commit groups with proof for each surface before merge.

options.title: Sponsor the full branch
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the broad review cost and own one bundled interactive-parity rollout after the paired PR clears proof and correctness blockers.

options.title: Defer or narrow
options.body: Maintainers can leave the roadmap open but reject or narrow parts that should wait for a smaller plugin/API or runtime design.

recommendation.title: Stage the rollout
recommendation.body: Keep this hub open and require focused question, plan, and goal PRs or commit groups with proof for each surface before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal for the strict-agentic and update_plan policy decisions that this roadmap extends.
